newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent extends losses on weaker NYMEX gasoline.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent extends losses on weaker NYMEX gasoline.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures extended losses on Friday after a weaker than expected start on NYMEX gasoline and losses in U.S. crude, brokers said.
September IPE Brent was down 12 cents at $18.57 a barrel at 1413 GMT, 12 cents off the low and 11 cents below the high of $18.68 touched late morning.
Unleaded gasoline dipped to 61.50 cents a gallon on the opening but crept back to 61.55. August NYMEX crude was down 12 cents at $19.87.
"There's nothing going on and no headlines. We're just following the States at the moment," a broker said.
IPE Brent's next upside resistance was at $18.78 and then $18.96. September bounced off support at $18.45 during morning trading.
IPE August gas oil was down $1 a tonne at $166 but above the day's $165.25 low.
Brokers had seen gasoline starting flat to 0.25 cent a gallon higher due to disruption of U.S. oil operations on the Gulf Coast from Hurricane Danny
Demand for oil products and a buoyant Brent cargo market provided a counterweight to several potentially bearish market factors including front month NYMEX crude's failure to breach $20.00 a barrel.
Brokers described as supportive the deferral of one Forties cargo to the August programme from July because of prblems at the Nelson field.
Other supportive factors included strong gasoline in the U.S., firm Asian naphtha and looming backwardation on Brent cargoes, said traders.
